subject: sleep
title: Your Brain's Night Shift
summary: What your brain does while you sleep, and how much sleep you need.

cards.title: A third of your life
cards.text: You spend about one-third of your life asleep. That sounds like a lot of doing nothing. But your brain is busy all night. What is it doing?

cards.title: Saving what you learned
cards.text: Sleep helps your brain build and keep the pathways it uses to learn and remember. Without enough sleep, it is harder to focus and to react quickly.
cards.example: So sleep is part of learning, not a break from it.

cards.title: A cleanup crew
cards.text: Scientists have found signs that sleep may help clean out waste that builds up in the brain while you are awake. They are still learning how it all works.

cards.title: Your body clock
cards.text: Your body has a clock that runs on about 24 hours. When it gets dark, your brain makes more of a chemical called melatonin, which helps you feel sleepy. Bright light, like from screens, can make it harder to fall asleep.

cards.title: How much do you need?
cards.text: Experts say kids ages 6 to 12 should sleep 9 to 12 hours a night. Teens need 8 to 10 hours. Grown-ups need 7 to 9.

cards.question: What is one thing that makes it harder for you to fall asleep? What is one small change you could try?
nudges: Think about light, screens, noise, and worries.

questions.q: Why is sleep important for learning?

options.text: It helps your brain build pathways to remember things.
options.why: Yes. Sleep helps lock in what you learned.
Your brain stays very active during sleep.

sources.title: Brain Basics: Understanding Sleep
sources.publisher: National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NIH)
sources.supports: We sleep about a third of our time; sleep is needed to form memory pathways; a possible "housekeeping" role; sleep stages and REM; circadian rhythm and sleep drive; adenosine, caffeine, melatonin, and light; the purpose of sleep is still partly a mystery.

sources.title: How Much Sleep Is Enough?
sources.publisher: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (NIH)
sources.supports: Recommended sleep: adults 7 to 9 hours; children 6 to 12, 9 to 12 hours; teens 13 to 18, 8 to 10 hours; adults sleeping under 7 hours may have more health issues.
